Let $s \in S$ be an arbitrary element. We evaluate the expression on the right-hand side at $s$:
\[ \left( \frac{1}{2} (f + g - |f - g|) \right)(s) = \frac{1}{2} \left( f(s) + g(s) - |f(s) - g(s)| \right) \]

We proceed by considering two cases for the relationship between the real numbers $f(s)$ and $g(s)$:

Case 1: Suppose $f(s) \le g(s)$. 
Then $f(s) - g(s) \le 0$, which implies that the absolute value $|f(s) - g(s)|$ is equal to $-(f(s) - g(s)) = g(s) - f(s)$.
Substituting this into our expression yields:
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{2} \left( f(s) + g(s) - |f(s) - g(s)| \right) &= \frac{1}{2} \left( f(s) + g(s) - (g(s) - f(s)) \right) \\
&= \frac{1}{2} \left( f(s) + g(s) - g(s) + f(s) \right) \\
&= \frac{1}{2} \left( 2f(s) \right) \\
&= f(s)
\end{align*}
Since $f(s) \le g(s)$, we have $\min\{f(s), g(s)\} = f(s)$. Thus, the right-hand side evaluated at $s$ equals $\min\{f(s), g(s)\}$.

Case 2: Suppose $f(s) > g(s)$.
Then $f(s) - g(s) > 0$, so $|f(s) - g(s)| = f(s) - g(s)$.
Substituting this into our expression yields:
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{2} \left( f(s) + g(s) - |f(s) - g(s)| \right) &= \frac{1}{2} \left( f(s) + g(s) - (f(s) - g(s)) \right) \\
&= \frac{1}{2} \left( f(s) + g(s) - f(s) + g(s) \right) \\
&= \frac{1}{2} \left( 2g(s) \right) \\
&= g(s)
\end{align*}
Since $f(s) > g(s)$, we have $\min\{f(s), g(s)\} = g(s)$. Thus, the right-hand side evaluated at $s$ equals $\min\{f(s), g(s)\}$.

In both cases, we have established that:
\[ \frac{1}{2} \left( f(s) + g(s) - |f(s) - g(s)| \right) = \min\{f(s), g(s)\} = (f \wedge g)(s) \]
Since $s \in S$ was chosen arbitrarily, the equality holds for all $s \in S$. 
Therefore, by the definition of equality of mappings, the functions themselves are equal:
\[ f \wedge g = \frac{1}{2} (f + g - |f - g|) \]
This completes the proof.
